subject: Security discovery: Medoro — retention / backups / deletion SLA clarifications

Subject: Security discovery: Medoro — retention / backups / deletion SLA clarifications

Hi Laura / Medoro Compliance team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the thorough run-through of your architecture and the specific questions on logs/backups and deletion SLAs. Per our conversation I wanted to summarize the open items and propose next steps so we have a clean handoff to our security ops and legal teams.

Quick recap of what we covered:
- Data types in scope: user-generated content for product features (notes, transcripts) + system metadata (timestamps, request/response logs).
- Logs: short-term streaming logs retained in-memory for 48–72 hours; aggregated request logs persisted for operational debugging and RPO/RTO analysis.
- Backups: daily snapshots of persisted data with 30-day rolling retention (subject to customer-configurable retention policy).
- Deletion: soft-delete + background purge; purge window dependent on retention class and backup restore windows.

Open questions you raised (we've numbered for reference):
1) Can Redwood provide an absolute maximum window between a user-initiated delete and the final irreversible erasure across all backups?
2) What are the guarantees around log accessibility for eDiscovery / audit (retention, format, exportability)?
3) Do we offer per-tenant retention overrides (shorter/longer) and how are those honored across snapshotting and off-site backups?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben (cc'd) will own collecting the backup/restore technical docs and a short diagram showing where snapshots live and how restore paths interact with soft-deletes.
- Monica (cc'd, Security) will initiate our vendor security questionnaire and provide the SOC 2 status & evidence pointers.
- Laura / Medoro team to confirm any regulatory constraints that would force a shorter retention or require special custody (HIPAA PHI notes, etc).

I attached the blank questionnaire we usually use to get the ball rolling; if you prefer we can start with the specific sections you care about (retention, backups, deletion) and redline.

Doc attachments: Medoro_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (fillable), backup_policy_diagram.png (high-level snapshot flow).

If that plan looks good, Ben and Monica will follow up by tomorrow with doc links and an ask-list for any evidence you might want to see (SOC 2 report date, encryption-at-rest key rotation cadence, backup lifecycle notes).

Thanks — Avery

Thanks Avery — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

On question (1): our legal/compliance team requires a worst-case maximum time to permanent erasure that accounts for off-site backups. Ideally that would be stated in contractual language (SLA or schedule). Can Redwood commit to a quantified max purge window or is that variable depending on the backup media and restore cadence?

On question (2): for audit purposes we need logs in a structured export (JSON or CSV) and the ability to provide a time-bounded export for a specific tenant. Is that supported today or would that require engineering work? Also please confirm whether request logs contain PII or are tokenized/hashed.

On question (3): we will likely need per-tenant shorter retention for certain customer classes (HIPAA PHI). Please confirm whether per-tenant retention is supported and if applying a shorter retention will prevent data from being included in snapshots/backups.

Happy to hop back on a short call if that will speed clarifications — otherwise please send the evidence and approximate timelines for any engineering work.

Best,
Laura

Subject: Re: Security discovery: Medoro — retention / backups / deletion SLA clarifications

Laura — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, then details and attachments.

1) Max purge window: We can commit contractually to a maximum irreversible erasure window of 45 days for primary data plus backups under our standard Private/Dedicated offering. That number reflects our backup snapshot rotation and typical off-site replication latencies. For Hosted customers we currently provide a 60-day maximum unless a Dedicated contract is in place (we can discuss a shorter SLA in an enterprise addendum).

2) Logs and exportability: We support time-bounded exports of request and audit logs in CSV/JSON today via our internal ops tool. Exports are tenant-scoped; we will provide a documented export procedure and a downloadable artifact for audits. Request logs are redacted for sensitive fields by default — any PII fields are hashed/obfuscated unless explicitly configured to persist raw values for troubleshooting (requires explicit customer opt-in and compliance review).

3) Per-tenant retention: Yes — per-tenant retention overrides are supported on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can enforce shorter retention windows via configuration flags tied to the tenant, but note that backups/snapshots operate at the storage level: when a snapshot includes a tenant with short retention, our restore procedures exclude soft-deleted records per the tenant policy; however, the snapshot binary will still exist until its retention expiry. Practically, that means irrecoverable erasure across all copies follows the purge window described above unless we agree to a bespoke contract to expedite off-site removal.

Attached: a short one-pager with the backup lifecycle and a pre-filled questionnaire section focused on retention & logs.

Action items:
- Monica: initiate the vendor security questionnaire; Laura please confirm the preferred format & whether you want us to pre-populate HIPAA-specific answers.
- Avery: please share proposed contractual language for the 45/60-day purge window so Medoro legal can review.

Laura — looping in the security ops intake and next steps. I started the vendor questionnaire in the attached spreadsheet and pre-filled answers for the sections we discussed (SOC 2 cert date, encryption details, backup cadence). A few notes for your team to review:

- SOC 2: Redwood last completed a Type II audit 2027-02-18; we can provide the secure report link and a cover letter.
- Encryption: all persisted customer data is AES-256 at rest; keys are rotated annually by default and managed through KMS. We offer HSM-backed key management for Private customers.
- Backups: daily snapshot with 30-day default retention; off-site replication to a second region within 24–72 hours depending on region pairing. Snapshots are retained according to tenant policy but physical removal from backup media follows the purge SLA above.

If Medoro can confirm which tenant classes require HIPAA-level retention overrides, I will flag those in the questionnaire and list any follow-up evidence (e.g., data flow diagrams, config screens) we need to provide.

I'll upload the questionnaire to the secure drive and send a DocuSign link for the confirmation of the 45-day purge SLA language once Avery shares the draft.

Thanks,
